dashboard.label: Escalation rules
dashboard.description: Site rules that lift a finding above what the score alone would give it, and what each one would move before you switch it on.

div.b: Every rule ships switched off, and this page is how you decide whether to switch one on.
div.span: An escalation rule re-orders the queue. It never invents a finding, never changes a CVE's severity and never lowers anything: a rule can only bump a finding up. The replay below runs every rule against the fleet as it stands right now and reports what would move, without moving anything.

A rule that names a fact the app does not compute cannot fire. It is not an error and it is not silently ignored either: the validator refuses it, and it shows here as moving nothing at all. Read "would move nothing" as either "no finding matches today" or "this rule is waiting on a measurement that does not exist yet" — the condition column tells you which.

panel.title: What each rule would move, replayed against the fleet now

search.query: | savedsearch "Riskability - replay escalation rules" | eval Move = from_tier . " to " . to_tier | rename rule AS Rule, enabled AS "On", findings AS Findings, hosts AS Hosts, cves AS CVEs | table Rule, "On", Move, Findings, Hosts, CVEs

div.span: A rule that would move thousands of findings is not thereby a good rule: it is a rule that has stopped discriminating, and a queue where everything is urgent is a queue with no order in it. The useful shape is a small number of findings moved for a reason you can state in one sentence.

search.query: | rest /servicesNS/nobody/riskability/configs/conf-riskability_escalations splunk_server=local | search title!="default" | rename title AS rule | eval rk_on = if(enabled="1", "yes", "no") | fields rule, rk_on, bump, when | append [ | savedsearch "Riskability - replay escalation rules" | stats sum(findings) AS rk_moves BY rule ] | stats values(rk_on) AS "On", values(bump) AS Bump, values(when) AS Condition, sum(rk_moves) AS rk_moves BY rule | eval "Would move" = if(coalesce(rk_moves, 0) > 0, rk_moves . " findings", "nothing today") | rename rule AS Rule | sort - rk_moves, Rule | table Rule, "On", Bump, "Would move", Condition

div.b: Bump is a number of tiers, not a score.
div.span: A rule moves a finding up that many tiers from wherever the deterministic score put it. It does not add points, so two rules firing on the same finding do not compound into an arbitrary number; the escalation cap and floor macros bound the result.

div.b: Rules live in a conf file, not in this page.
div.span: Add a stanza to local/riskability_escalations.conf with a when condition, a bump, and enabled = 0 until the replay above tells you what it does. The fields a condition may name are allowlisted and typed, and the spec file README/riskability_escalations.conf.spec lists every one of them along with whether the app actually computes it today.

Graded fields are strings on purpose, so a condition can only name the grade it means. Ordering comparisons are refused on them: "unknown" is the absence of a measurement, not a low value on the same scale as the real grades, and a rule allowed to write > against it would be placing absence somewhere on a scale it does not belong to.
